conviction_note: Seven small findings that partly cancel, summing to +0.6: a guided-down Q1 bar from a team that beat its own guide all of FY26, and EU-4 2026 contract prices fixed 15-25% below last year, set against soft QSR traffic and a 4% YoY build in US fry inventory. The direction will be set by whether management holds the FY27 $1.1-1.2B EBITDA guide despite the European crop, and nothing I found answers that. Since the evidence leans against a -20.7% 20-day run-up and defensive options flow, the emitted number is cut by a third below the sum, to +0.4.
bar: Company Q1 FY27 guide from the Q4 FY26 call (2026-07-24): net sales flat and adjusted EBITDA down low teens, against a Q1 FY26 base of $1,659.3M sales and $302.2M adj. EBITDA, i.e. about $1.66B and $260-268M. Consensus agrees: EPS $0.584 and revenue $1.654B (MarketBeat 2026-09-29), $0.58 (ad-hoc-news 2026-09-28), with a range of $0.58-0.62 across sources. Sources: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068 and https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/upcoming-lamb-weston-lw-expected-to-announce-earnings-on-tuesday-2026-09-29/
positioning_check: Short interest 6.66M shares (4.8% of shares), 5.08 days to cover at the 2026-09-15 settlement, up from 6.29M / 4.77 DTC on 2026-08-31 (https://equibles.com/stocks/lw/short-interest). Ortex puts it at 4.7% of free float with very loose borrow, and the put/call ratio at 2.08, more than 2 SD above its 20-day average of 0.91, after reading below 0.63 in mid-September (https://ortex.news/articles/177222/lamb-weston-heads-into-earnings-with-options-traders-at-peak-caution, late Sept 2026). The baseline chain is unusable: no 25-delta skew, and the 8.43 put/call open-interest ratio sits on only 66 contracts. So the defensive positioning is in options, not crowded shorts, and there is no squeeze mechanism to lean on.

findings.finding: Lamb Weston itself guided Q1 FY27 to flat sales and adj. EBITDA down low teens (about $260-268M against $302.2M). The same management team beat its own FY26 guide (adj. EBITDA $1,147M against a top end of $1,140M; sales $6,612M against $6,550M) and beat Q4 consensus EPS by 38% ($0.87 against $0.63), so the Q1 bar was set by a team that has been sandbagging.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A 38% EPS beat with sales above guide on 2026-07-24 moved the stock +0.81% (baseline). The Q1 FY26 print on 2025-09-30, a beat with the FY guide reaffirmed, moved it +4.33%. This name does not pay much for a reported-quarter beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS of $0.58 already sits at the guided EBITDA decline, so the street has taken the guide at face value rather than adjusting for the team's beat pattern. If it had, the Q1 EPS range would be skewed above $0.62, and analysts would not have spent the last week cutting price targets (JPM $52 to $46 on 09-30, Stephens $55 to $50 on 09-28).
findings.independence: The Q1 guide quote comes from a different document, the Q4 call transcript: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lamb-weston-tops-q4-2026-estimates-as-volume-rises-93CH-4812068. The beat history and the guide are one management track record, counted once.

findings.finding: DCA Market Intelligence reports that most of the EU-4 2026 processing crop was pre-contracted at prices about 25% below last year for early delivery and 15-17% below for storage delivery. Meanwhile the free-buy fries quote went from EUR 0/100kg in spring to about EUR 20/100kg. So in FY27 contracted processors like Lamb Weston hold a cost advantage over spot buyers, the reverse of FY26, when competitors bought near-free potatoes and LW took a $33.1M potato write-off. That cuts against the 'deteriorating European crop raises LW procurement cost' thesis that Stephens put out on 09-28 and that the stock sold off on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: FY-guide changes are what move this stock: the guide cuts in Dec 2024 and Dec 2025 brought -20.1% and -25.94%, while the reaffirm on 2025-09-30 brought +4.33% (baseline). International hit Q4 FY26 EBITDA (-81%) and the 2026-07-24 reaction was still only +0.81%.
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 7.4% in 5 days and 20.7% in 20 days, and the only named cause is Stephens' crop-cost framing; JPM followed with a cut two days later. If the market had weighed contract coverage at 15-25% lower prices against the yield shortfall, the late-September leg would not have happened on a note that names only the shortfall. The caveat is netted into the size: lower yields mean contracted volumes under-deliver and the gap is bought at about EUR 200/t spot, which is why the range runs negative.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not an LW number, and no LW document confirms how it transmits. A separate source has the Belgian/Dutch fries quotes at EUR 20/100kg with processors 'pulling out all the stops' on small tubers: https://www.nieuweoogst.nl/nieuws/2026/09/28/potatonl-haalt-kaasschaaf-langs-aardappelnoteringen (2026-09-28). Processors 'largely supplied from contracted volumes': https://commodity-board.com/eu-4-potato-harvest-slumps-contracts-delay-full-price-shock (2026-09-29). Against: Stephens via https://www.investing.com/news/analyst-ratings/stephens-cuts-lamb-weston-stock-price-target-on-europe-concerns-93CH-4919969.

findings.finding: US restaurant demand during LW's Q1 (Jun-Aug 2026) was soft at QSR, with Placer.ai visits down 3.4% YoY in both July and August and total dining down 2.4% in August, but firmer in other channels: Darden's quarter to 2026-08-30 had blended same-restaurant sales up 3.1%, and broadline distributors grew cases (Sysco US foodservice +2.5%, US Foods independents +5.1%) in the April-June quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q4 FY26 (Mar-May), Placer had May QSR traffic at -4.4%, yet LW posted +7% total volume (North America sales +9%) on share gains, and the stock moved +0.81%. Traffic softness has not shown up in LW's own volume.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Simply Wall St (2026-09-10) cites weaker restaurant traffic as a reason for the early-September slide. What is new since the guide is that July and August QSR traffic stayed around -3.4% with no recovery. Sized small because LW's own volume grew through a -4.4% traffic month, a company-level number that contradicts the proxy.
findings.independence: July QSR -3.4%: https://www.placer.ai/anchor/articles/retail-and-dining-index-july-2026-retail-keeps-its-edge. Darden counterweight: https://investor.darden.com/news/news-details/2026/Darden-Restaurants-Reports-Fiscal-2027-First-Quarter-Results-Declares-Quarterly-Dividend-and-Reaffirms-Fiscal-2027-Outlook/default.aspx. McDonald's Q2 US guest counts negative: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/04/mcdonalds-mcd-q2-2026-earnings.html

findings.finding: US french-fry stocks in cold storage were 1,017.5M lb on 2026-08-31, 104% of a year earlier. They built 48.2M lb over Jun-Aug 2026 (from 969.3M on May 31), against 23.4M lb in the same months of 2025. That points to industry supply running ahead of sell-through in LW's Q1 and to pressure on NA price/mix going into contract renewals.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The NA price/mix line drove the Dec 2025 (-25.94%) and Dec 2024 (-20.1%) reactions (baseline), but those were Q2 prints, when contracts and crop are set. Q1 prints have not carried a pricing reset in this history.
findings.why_not_priced: NASS Cold Storage is a free government series that no LW preview or analyst note cites. If the market had read it, the NA pricing worry would be in the price-target notes, which mention only Europe. Part of the build may be LW deliberately pre-building ahead of the Dutch plant closure or new-crop changeover, so it is sized as a proxy.
findings.independence: The May 31 comparison is from a different NASS release: https://esmis.nal.usda.gov/sites/default/release-files/795951/cost0626.pdf. Consistent with the QSR traffic finding, but a separate series.

findings.finding: US frozen potato exports fell 14.6% YoY in June 2026 (Japan -15.5%, Philippines -41%, Saudi Arabia -85%), and the July 2025-June 2026 marketing year had total US potato exports down 4.8% in volume. International volume was weak going into LW's Q1.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: International weakness (Q4 FY26 segment EBITDA -81%, Middle East) came with a +0.81% reaction on 2026-07-24. The market has looked through this line.
findings.source_date: June 2026 monthly data (snippet_only; the page did not render on fetch)
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly inside the guide: management already flagged Middle East volume headwinds and competitive EMEA and Asia pressure. What is new is the scale of the Japan and Philippines declines, where cheaper Chinese and Indian fries are displacing US product. Sized small because it lands inside what was guided.
findings.independence: Marketing-year total: https://www.freshplaza.com/north-america/article/9868241/u-s-potato-exports-reach-2-99-million-tons-in-2025-26/ (one shared underlying Potatoes USA / Census dataset).

findings.finding: LW goes into its Q1 print, historically the reaffirm print (2025-09-30 'Reaffirms Fiscal Year 2026 Outlook', +4.33%), down 20.7% in 20 days and 37% off its high. The defensive positioning is in options (put/call 2.08, more than 2 SD above average), while short interest is a modest 4.8% and insiders bought about $19.3M over the trailing 12 months. A hold of the FY27 range, with the crop update deferred to the December print, would land against hedged rather than crowded-long positioning.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A Q1 reaffirm brought +4.33% (2025-09-30). The large negatives in the baseline (-25.94%, -20.1%, -8.94%) all came at Q2/Q3 prints with guide changes.
findings.source_date: 2026-09-29 (approx., 'reports in eight days' context; page states JPM and Stephens cut 'this week')
findings.why_not_priced: The option market's directional statement is bearish and that is the lean this finding has to beat. The reason it may be wrong for this print is timing: LW sets crop and pricing at the December print, and in July management guided Q1 as the weak quarter, with growth to 'ramp through the remainder of the year'. Sized small because this is close to 'down a lot with puts bid', which by itself is not a finding.

findings.finding: The Broekhuizenvorst (Netherlands) plant closure carries $80-110M of pre-tax charges, mostly in FY27, with at least 20% in cash. Q1 GAAP will carry part of it, and it is excluded from the adjusted metrics.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Restructuring charges have been adjusted out and have not moved the stock on their own in this history.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced: disclosed in an 8-K under Item 2.05, below adjusted operating profit, and with no path to the guide beyond the capacity cut that the guide already reflects.

outside_window.finding: Investor day planned for early calendar 2027, with an update on Focus to Win, which targets $250M annualised savings by FY28.
Full impact of the European 2026 crop on contract prices for the 2027 crop and on fry pricing. Under LW's own cadence the crop and pricing assessment lands at the Q2 (December) print.

rejected_candidates.detail: Merged into the European contract-price finding (as the thesis it cuts against) and the positioning finding

baseline_tension: The evidence leans mildly positive, which cuts against the -20.7% 20-day run-up and the bearish options flow (put/call 2.08), though the baseline has no usable skew number. The positives are an industry proxy and a reaction-timing argument rather than a company document, so the emitted move is smaller than the sum.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (fact is not reaction): the Q1 bar/beat finding went from +1.0 to +0.5, because a 38% EPS beat bought only +0.81% on 2026-07-24.
Rule 5 (proxy and inference sized below documents): the EU-4 contract-price finding went from +1.5 to +1.0, since it is industry-level reasoning from crop and contract data with no LW confirmation.

Rule 5 and rule 3: the QSR traffic finding went from -1.0 to -0.4. LW's own +7% volume (NA sales +9%) through a -4.4% traffic month contradicts the proxy, and the Darden and broadline counterweight was netted in rather than left in the text.
Rule 6 (inside the guide): the export finding went from -0.5 to -0.3, because Middle East and international weakness were already in the Q1 guide.
Rule 7 (positioning is the thing to beat): the positioning finding went from +1.5 to +0.7, because its sign is against the bearish options flow and it sits close to 'down a lot with puts bid'.
Cold storage finding: -1.0 to -0.8, a mild trim for possible deliberate inventory pre-build. It is a broad government series, so rule 5 did not cut it further.

Rule 3 (caveat reaches the number): baseline_tension says the set leans against the run-up and options flow, so expected_move went from +1.5 to +0.4, below the +0.6 sum. The Dutch closure one-off (-0.1) was left unchanged.
